To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

benzaldehyde is an effective synergist for the aggregation pheromonal component of the plum curculio pheromone and that benzaldehyde and the pheromone can be released at low rates (10 and 1 mg/day, respectively) from traps to attract plum curculios to traps.

the combination of benzaldehyde and grandisoic acid was attractive to overwintered adults of Conotrachelus nemuphar in Massachusetts and that this combination may be useful in monitoring traps for plum curculios.
benzaldehyde at 10 mg/ day + grandisoic acid at 1 mg/ day of release is an attractive lure that can improve the effectiveness of plum curculio monitoring traps.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an effective monitoring tool to improve timing of PC insecticide applications and to facilitate development and implementation of IPM tactics.
the development of an improved trap that may be used to monitor PC populations in apple orchards.
developing a lure that will enhance the effectiveness of monitoring programs for PCs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the attractiveness of the pheromone alone was not enhanced by the presence and/or amount of host odors, but the attractiveness of host odors was enhanced by the presence (and amount) of the pheromic.
the attractiveness of a combination of GA and BEN to PC is not consistent, and that the response of PC to this combination is dependent upon trap design.

the attractiveness of a synthetic aggregation phermone, GA, is not enhanced when combined with other plant volatiles, and that the most attractive lure for PCs is the binary combination of GA at 1-2 mg/day and benzaldehyde at 10 mg/ day of release.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of benzaldehyde and GA is a good lure for monitoring PCs in Massachusetts.
the combination of BEN and GA was the most attractive lure for PCs.
the combination of GA + BEN at the release rates described here may be used as an attractant in traps to monitor PCs in orchards.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the attractiveness of synthetic pheromones and synthetic host odors to overwintered PCs can be enhanced by combining them in traps.

the attractiveness of synthetic host volatiles and the synthetic aggregation phermonone grandisoic acid (GA) to overwintering adult plum curculio (PC), Conotrachelu s nenuphar, was examined using two trap types: sticky panels and black pyramidal traps.
a binary combination of a pheromone and host odor can enhance the response of a pest to a pheromonal bait.
